text:
Kent Johnson scored on about a 2% chance, and that was enough. His wrist shot at 3:26 of overtime ended a game CBJ had spent regulation mostly surviving, and it handed the Blue Jackets a 1-0 win at Nationwide Arena. By expected goals, NYR created 3.51 to CBJ's 3.36, and the replay model gave NYR a 52% chance of deserving the win to CBJ's 48%.

The reason it stayed close was Jet Greaves. He turned aside all 29 shots, which by the numbers was 3.51 goals better than the chances he faced would normally allow. NYR's best look came in the third period, when Pavel Dorofeyev had a 40% chance and missed the net. Gabe Perreault led the visitors with six shots on goal and 0.82 expected goals of his own, but nothing got through. NYR outpaced CBJ 67 to 57 in shot attempts and 2.83 to 1.91 at even strength, yet neither power play converted, each going 0 for 3.

Overtime was the one stretch CBJ clearly controlled, out-chancing NYR 0.65 to 0.12 in expected goals. Johnson's shot, set up by Zach Werenski and Charlie Coyle, was the payoff. At the other end, Dylan Garand stopped 28 of 29 and saved 2.36 goals above expectation, which is why a loss this tight never felt like a blowout. For CBJ, it was a night to credit the goalie and take the point.
